before.title: Demand pattern
before.body: Aloft demand follows market seasonality plus Bonvoy campaign calendars. Treat portfolio averages as directional only until property pace data exists.

before.title: Competitive pressure
before.body: Same-market Marriott sister brands can both help (Bonvoy shoppers) and cannibalize. Map sister-brand density before assuming exclusive Bonvoy capture for Aloft.

before.title: Conversion workstream
before.body: Systems, content, and rate integrity at cutover determine whether platform demand actually books the hotel in week one.

before.title: What is differentiated commercially
before.body: Lifestyle select-service Marriott brand with loft-inspired public space and tech-forward guest journey inside Marriott Bonvoy. Commercially, the brand case is Bonvoy + Marriott channels applied to a distinct Aloft product — not a generic Marriott International story.

before.title: Commercial engine
before.body: Aloft Hotels sells through Marriott International distribution and Marriott Bonvoy while the brand product must still win the stay. Commercial diligence should separate platform reach from Aloft conversion on the property.

after.title: Commercial Engine
after.body: Aloft Hotels commercial distribution rides Marriott Bonvoy direct channels, GDS, OTAs, and parent sales systems. Select-service lifestyle: modern rooms, social lobby energy, and tech-forward cues for urban and airport-adjacent travelers inside Marriott Bonvoy. Owners should underwrite channel mix and loyalty contribution for this asset—not corporate averages alone.
